topic: How does the 45° scan range affect link budget calculations for edge-of-coverage users compared to broadside beams?
consensus_response: The 45° scan range increases path loss for edge-of-coverage users due to increased angle of incidence and distance between the satellite and user, reducing available signal power. This degrades Quality of Service (QoS) and capacity. Broadside beams minimize interference but have a narrower 22.5° scan, affecting coverage. Adaptive beamforming can mitigate these issues by dynamically adjusting beam patterns, but requires complex resource allocation algorithms and may introduce additional overhead. Atmospheric effects like rain fade and ionospheric scintillation further increase path loss, impacting edge-of-coverage users more significantly with the 45° scan range.
